title: I'm a UX Designer who's been experimenting with AI-assisted game development
author: starmakereden
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I wanted to share a project I've been working on 🐱

It's a playful 3D game where you become a house cat trying to get internet famous by doing everyday cat things, from making biscuits and squeezing into cardboard boxes to knocking things over and creating absolute chaos.

I've been building it in **Godot**, using **Codex to assist with programming, prototyping and debugging**, while I focus on game design, UX, creative direction and playtesting.

One of the most interesting parts has been seeing how actual players interact with the game. I've gone through several rounds of playtesting, and some of the biggest changes came from watching people struggle with things I thought were obvious.

For example, I initially leaned heavily into destructive cat behaviour, but playtesting helped me realise that simply being an adorable cat could be just as entertaining. That eventually shaped the game's three content categories: **Cozy, Chaos and Destruction**.

AI has helped me move much faster with implementation, but it hasn't replaced the need to design, test, identify problems and iterate. I've also had my fair share of debugging sessions where AI-generated code needed multiple revisions.

The game is now publicly playable on itch.io! It's still a work in progress, with some unfinished visuals and occasional bugs.

🎮 **Play my game here:** [https://katescapedsgn.itch.io/cloutandcatnip](https://katescapedsgn.itch.io/cloutandcatnip)

I'd love to hear from other AI-assisted game developers: **how are you balancing AI-generated implementation with your own creative and design decisions?**
